title: Self-training for cross-centre coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography using pre-contrast frame subtraction
mechanism: Self-train on a target-centre pool. Pixels found only by an independent physical cue (pre-contrast subtraction) are set to ignore, not background. The gain depends on how sensitive the teacher is.
adaptation: E1 analogue: pool = CSIR half-cut cells. Pseudo-labels come from the PF ensemble. Pixels flagged only by a ridge filter (black top-hat or Frangi tuned to the 4 px FWHM crack profile) become ignore, so cracks the teacher misses are not taught as background.
min_experiment: Arm ST-ignore vs plain target-pool self-training vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack recall and relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03 over PF.
evidence: R: thin-vessel segmentation, ARCADE -> XCAD/XACV. XCAD macro Dice +2.7 (95% CI 2.3 to 3.2); a same-epoch fine-tuning control gave -0.6. A second round gave no gain. Starting from a 50-image model, XCAD Dice went 0.623 -> 0.745; XACV did not improve where main vessels were missed.
prior_overlap: Our Mean Teacher with the external pool set unlabelled pixels by teacher argmax and used no ignore cue. It was not aimed at E1. Open. Risk: E1 crack recall is 0.17, which is the paper's failure case.
